# 2026-07-26 · Carry settlement currency on the order

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T22:26:19+09:00`
Risk: R2
Status: In progress

## Problem and intended outcome

Two partners onboarding this quarter settle in currencies other than USD.
Today the currency is implied by the partner and hard-coded at the reporting
layer, which is already wrong for one existing partner and is worked around by
hand each month.

Intended outcome: the settlement currency is stored on the order itself
rather than derived, the adapter sends it with the payload, and reporting
reads it from the row instead of a lookup table.

Constraint: historic rows must backfill to USD, which is correct for every
order placed so far.

## Success and non-goals

Success: reporting no longer hard-codes currency, and the currency shown for
any order (past or future) matches the agreement in force when it was
placed.

Not in scope: renegotiating currency for existing agreements, or changing how
amounts are stored (still integer cents, see
`docs/engineering/decisions/partner-settlement-rounding.md`).

## Existing responsibilities searched

`src/db/schema.py` owns the orders table definition — extended with
`settlement_currency TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'` rather than a new table.
`src/api/partner_adapter.py::to_partner_payload` owns the settlement payload
shape and is the single place the currency is added to the outbound payload.
A per-partner currency lookup table was considered and rejected (see ADR):
currency is a property of the agreement in force when the order was placed,
not of the partner today, so deriving it would lose history once an
agreement changes. The reporting read path referenced in the proposal is not
present in this repository checkout; it is out of scope for this change
record and should be picked up when that code is located.

## System and data flow

Order row (`settlement_currency` column) -> `to_partner_payload` -> partner
settlement API. Separately: order row -> reporting read path (currently
hard-coded, to be updated once located).

## Decisions and trade-offs

See `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`: store currency on
the order rather than a per-partner table.

## Failure, security, and recovery

A missing or wrong currency on an order causes reporting/settlement to use
the wrong unit, misstating amounts rather than failing loudly. Rollback for
the schema change is dropping the column; the default keeps existing writers
working during rollout. No secrets or auth are involved.

## Verification evidence

`unit` (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`) passed 2026-07-26 against
the current diff (schema change for step 1; step 3 adapter change not yet
made).

## Known limits and learning gaps

Reporting read path (plan step 4) and removal of the reporting hard-code
(step 5) are not started, and the reporting module's location in this repo
is unresolved.

## References

- Proposal: `docs/proposals/settlement-currency.md`
- Plan: `plans/settlement-currency.md`
- ADR: `docs/engineering/decisions/settlement-currency.md`

# 2026-07-26 · Carry settlement currency on the order

Change ID: `settlement-currency`
Created: `2026-07-26T22:26:19+09:00`
Status: Accepted

## Context

Settlement currency is currently implied by the partner and hard-coded at
the reporting layer. That is already wrong for one existing partner and two
more partners onboarding this quarter settle in non-USD currencies.

## Options considered

1. Per-partner currency lookup table.
2. Store settlement currency as a column on the order row.

## Decision

Choose option 2. Currency is a property of the agreement in force when the
order was placed, not of the partner today. A lookup table keyed by partner
loses that once an agreement changes currency; a column on the order
preserves the value that was true at order time. Historic rows backfill to
USD, which is correct for every order placed so far.

## Consequences and reversal

Every writer of an order row must supply (or default to) a currency; the
column defaults to `'USD'` so existing writers keep working unmodified during
rollout. Reversal is dropping the column and returning to the hard-coded
reporting value. Cost: reporting and the adapter now each read currency from
the row instead of a single hard-coded constant, so both must be kept in
sync with what the schema stores.

## Implementation references

- `src/db/schema.py`
- `src/api/partner_adapter.py` (pending: currency not yet added to payload)

## Supersession

Supersedes: None
Superseded by: None
